threads.body: [General] Client disconnects also affect commands other than `SHUTDOWN`. Closing a Lettuce 5.1 connection with a pending `BLPOP` produces a client failure whose `Connection closed` message reaches tracing without a throwable. This guard misses it, so the new prefix parser reports `error.type="Connection"` on spans and duration metrics instead of the exception-class fallback. Handle message-only client disconnects for ordinary commands without treating custom server replies as disconnects, and add a regression test that closes a connection with an outstanding command.

replies.body: Message-only callbacks no longer classify `Connection closed` as a server prefix. The pending-`BLPOP` disconnect regression checks both spans and duration metrics. A supplied exception retains its class fallback. The older Lettuce 5.x message-only SPI exposes neither the throwable nor enough information to distinguish server and client failures, so that path intentionally uses `_OTHER` rather than inventing an exception class. The README documents this limitation.

threads.body: [General] In Lettuce 5.1's message-only tracing path, a genuine server reply such as `ERR upstream failed. Command timed out after 100 millisecond(s)` matches this substring check. An EVAL script can return it through `redis.error_reply`, causing both the span and duration metric to report `RedisCommandTimeoutException` instead of `ERR`. Distinguish client timeout completions from server replies rather than searching arbitrary reply details, and add an EVAL regression test asserting both error labels.

threads.body: [General] The round-trip check validates the entire reply, although only its prefix contributes to `error.type`. With legacy decoding, UTF-8 `échec details` followed by byte `0xff` fails this check, so spans and duration metrics receive `ￃﾩchec` instead of `échec`. Extract the ASCII-space-delimited prefix before recovering and validating its bytes, while preserving empty/space-only replies as failures. Add a regression test combining a valid multibyte prefix with invalid detail bytes.

replies.body: This refers to the byte-recovery implementation that has been removed. The current implementation deliberately uses actual-exception-class fallback, or `_OTHER` when the message-only tracing SPI cannot distinguish server and client failures. We are not reconstructing legacy bytes, so the whole-message round-trip issue no longer applies.

threads.body: [General] A successful transactional `GET` can return a `Throwable` as application data through a custom `RedisCodec`, such as a codec that deserializes stored exceptions. Lettuce 6.x `MultiOutput` places successful decoded values in the same result list as command failures, so `instanceof Throwable` does not distinguish the two. This branch incorrectly marks a successful `EXEC` as failed and records the value's class as `error.type` on its span and duration metric; it can also hide a later actual failure. Use the constituent commands' failure information rather than the decoded values' Java types, and add a regression test for a successful transaction with a Throwable-valued codec.

@copilot Fix the newly identified successful-transaction misclassification in this existing PR.

The review thread is https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20793#discussion_r4344461657. At current head 912aaf9051356f6a78654da1cacdc8d305c60d9f, OpenTelemetryTracing.OpenTelemetrySpan.finishFromOutput() scans MultiOutput.get() and treats the first value instanceof Throwable as an EXEC failure.

This is not a reliable failure discriminator. A supported custom RedisCodec can deserialize a stored exception and legitimately return a Throwable as the successful value of GET. The published Lettuce 6.0.0.RELEASE implementations confirm the complete path: ValueOutput.set(ByteBuffer) stores codec.decodeValue(bytes); MultiOutput.complete() appends output.get() for successful constituent commands and execution exceptions for failed ones into the same responses list; AsyncCommand completes normally when the output has no error. The new scan therefore incorrectly marks a successful EXEC failed and labels its span and duration metric with the application value's class. It also returns before a later real failure, hiding the actual failure.

replies.body: I verified the Lettuce 6.0 and 6.5 APIs. `MultiOutput` checks each constituent `CommandOutput.hasError()` internally, then materializes either the successful `output.get()` value or an exception in the same `TransactionResult` list. The public `TransactionResult` API exposes no per-element failure flag, and `OpenTelemetryTracing` receives only the outer output at EXEC completion. Thus, once values are exposed through this API, a decoded `Throwable` cannot reliably be distinguished from an error result; class or message checks would remain incorrect. Recovering the constituent flags would require tracking commands across MULTI/EXEC outside the tracing callback contract. I can’t make a safe, focused fix with the supported API, so I left the code and its existing mixed-failure assertions unchanged.
